row.reason: Both sell subscription-based lead generation, SEO and digital marketing to local businesses. They differ in the core product and the customer vertical. Thryv sells a small-business management SaaS platform plus done-for-you marketing to home and local service providers. Cars.com runs a consumer car marketplace and sells listings, advertising and software to car dealers and automakers. Overlap exists in marketing services and local-business customers, but it is not full overlap in both.

C:S1.1.text: One analysis says the company earns most of its revenue from subscription advertising and listing packages sold to dealers, with smaller streams from dealer software, wholesale auction fees, and OEM media campaigns.

C:S2.1.text: Advertising is the second pillar. Brands and manufacturers use the platform to reach in-market shoppers.

C:S3.1.text: Cars.com connects shoppers and dealers. It acts as neutral digital infrastructure for traditional auto dealers rather than a direct competitor buying and selling cars itself.

C:S4.1.text: Display advertising on the marketplace sites, plus search engine optimization and search engine monetization programs for dealers, helps with media spend beyond the platform.

C:S5.1.text: Premium placements also appear as an option, with enhanced visibility for specific listings sold as premium packages.
